summary: On Wednesday, President Donald Trump proposed new tariffs on 14 trading partners, including China, the European Union, Japan, and India, targeting trade practices Washington claims burden American commerce.

Administration officials claim the new levies address 'overcapacity'—excess industrial production supported by government subsidies—which they argue allows cheaper goods to flood global markets and undercut American producers.
These duties fall under Section 301 of the Trade Act, targeting unfair trade practices. CNBC reported the tariffs are 'country specific' and will not stack on existing duties, except for China.
China faces a 20% tariff on top of the 25% imposed in 2018. If it fails to uphold the trade truce agreed in Busan, South Korea, in Oct. 2025, duties could jump to 40%.
Dismissing the 'overcapacity' claims, China asserted the condition does not exist. Trade Representative Jamieson Greer is scheduled to discuss the strategy on Squawk Box at 8.10 a.m. ET.
title: Source Icon

summary: On Wednesday, the Army intentionally detonated the nation's entire 5-ton stockpile of lead azide at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant in Middletown after officials determined the degrading chemicals posed an uncontrolled explosion risk.

Staff discovered during a March inspection that decades-old chemicals had crystallized, becoming sensitive to friction and cold temperatures. "Inaction is no longer an option," said Maj. Gen. Eric Shirley, the Army's leader of the operation.

The Army utilized 'blast barriers,' concrete walls, and ballistic gels while planning to douse the 68 barrels with over 100,000 gallons of water. Officials advised residents within 5 miles to evacuate.

A court ruling on Monday allowed the operation to proceed despite environmentalists' legal challenges. Nearby schools closed for the Thanksgiving holiday, while some residents sealed windows to guard against potential lead dust.

While the plume was expected to drift southwest toward Missouri, away from Burlington, residents remain anxious. "I don't think lead danger goes away any time soon," said Lucy Giehl, who lives nearby in West Burlington.
title: US Army carries out controlled blast of degraded explosives in Iowa

Official State Department travel advisories warn Americans against visiting Honduras' Gracias a Dios region due to violent crime, yet reports describe that same area as having low crime and functioning services.

Asylum attorney Neela Chakravartula of the Center for Gender & Refugee Studies argued the reports ignore asylum law, stating 'pockets of a country that are relatively safe doesn't mean everybody can just move.'

These six-page documents replace lengthy human rights dissections of more than 100 nations, while the State Department and The Justice Department declined to comment on the reports' role in asylum court decisions.
title: State Department Downplays Danger Facing Asylum Seekers: AP Probe

summary: The Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade is set to hold its 100th procession through New York City on Thursday, November 26, 2026, running from 8:30 a.m. to noon EST.
Although the event debuted in 1924—meaning its 100th calendar anniversary occurred in 2024—a three-year pause during World War II from 1942 to 1944 makes this year's march the official 100th edition.

To mark the milestone, Macy’s is deploying a record 100 inflatable elements, pairing new character balloons like Bluey, Sorcerer’s Apprentice Mickey, and Hello Kitty Big Apple with archival returns such as the Blue Hippopotamus and Blue Sky Gallery designs by Jeff Koons, Keith Haring, Yayoi Kusama, and Tim Burton.

Seven new floats are debuting for the centennial—including Macy’s Tony Sarg’s Amazing Marionettes, Hogwarts Holiday, and the Macy’s All-Stars float featuring classic parade figures like Bugs Bunny, Popeye, and Curious George.

The broadcast on NBC, Telemundo, and Peacock will feature headline performances at Herald Square by Teddy Swims and Megan Moroney, alongside float appearances by Queen Latifah, Jimmy Fallon & The Roots, DEVO, Wyclef Jean, and Leslie Odom Jr.
title: Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade Set for 100th Procession Through New York

summary: On Tuesday, a federal grand jury in Los Angeles indicted Thomas Markle Sr. on two counts of possessing child sexual abuse material, with the 82-year-old facing a statutory minimum of 20 years in federal prison if convicted.

Earlier this month, FBI agents seized approximately 78 items, including 35 mm film negatives, from Markle's two Los Angeles storage units; the indictment alleges he "knowingly" possessed images of children in sexually explicit poses.

The investigation began after Thomas Markle Jr. allegedly discovered a hoard of material at their former home in Cebu, Philippines; a witness later "positively identified the adult man as Markle," according to the criminal complaint.

Currently held in Florida, Markle was ordered to remain in custody this month for violating house arrest conditions after cutting his ankle monitor, with arraignment in Los Angeles expected in the coming weeks.

The Duchess of Sussex, Meghan Markle , previously described herself as "deeply distressed" by the "disturbing allegations" against her father, whose relationship with her has been strained since he missed her 2018 wedding to Prince Harry.

Federal authorities wrongly deported Abrego Garcia to El Salvador's CECOT prison in March 2025 as an "administrative error," then pursued him with a human smuggling indictment later dismissed by a judge as "vindictive."

After the Supreme Court ordered his return, the administration unsuccessfully pursued deportation to Liberia, Uganda, and Ghana; his legal team rejected these attempts and his preferred alternative, Costa Rica, was rejected by officials.

Maryland Senator Chris Van Hollen hailed Abrego Garcia as a "free man," while attorney Simon Sandoval-Moshenberg noted he avoided deportation "in shackles" on an ICE flight to Liberia the administration had planned.

Attorney Simon Sandoval-Moshenberg characterized the departure as temporary while Abrego Garcia "waits out the end of this administration," with plans to seek family reunification in Maryland under a future government.

summary: On Tuesday, a federal jury in Brooklyn convicted Huawei and three affiliates on 10 of 12 criminal counts, including bank fraud and conspiracy to steal trade secrets, though jurors acquitted the company of racketeering conspiracy.

Prosecutors alleged Huawei engaged in a decades-long conspiracy to steal trade secrets from American companies while deceptively concealing its business dealings in Iran from international banks to maintain access to U.S. financial systems.

Defense attorney Brian Heberlig argued prosecutors relied on "innuendo and facts ripped out of context," maintaining Huawei succeeded through "hard work, innovation, and investment in research and development" rather than coordinated criminality.

U.S. District Judge Ann Donnelly scheduled sentencing for September 14, 2027, when Huawei faces potential financial penalties including fines, asset forfeiture, and restitution as the company vowed to appeal the convictions.

Despite the verdict, experts note Huawei has diversified into artificial intelligence and chipmaking, remaining a key player in China's technology sector even as the company remains effectively excluded from the U.S. telecommunications market.
title: China's Huawei convicted in US in sprawling criminal trial over Iran business

summary: On Tuesday, the Associated Press declared Democrat Victoria Broderick the winner of Tennessee 's 4th Congressional District, giving Democrats 259 House seats—the largest majority for the party this century.

The contest was a rematch against Republican incumbent Scott DesJarlais, who defeated Broderick with 70% of the vote in 2024 before state lawmakers redrew district boundaries to increase competitiveness.
Confirming the result required a weeks-long count of provisional ballots because the margin was fewer than 400 votes out of about 196,000 cast, a gap of just 0.18 percentage points.
DesJarlais conceded days before the official call, writing on Facebook that he had "personally reached out to Ms. Broderick to offer my congratulations" on her new undertaking.
Three House races remain uncalled—one in Minnesota and two in Louisiana—with final results to arrive before Congress convenes in January, potentially enlarging the Democratic majority further.
title: Democrat Victoria Broderick Flips Tennessee's 4th District, Giving Party 259 House Seats

summary: On Monday, former Vice President Albert Gore announced he is purchasing the 113-year-old Carthage Courier, a weekly newspaper serving his Tennessee hometown and Smith County.
The acquisition ends five decades of ownership by the family of Hershel and Geraldine Lake, who listed the Carthage Courier for sale earlier this fall before Geraldine's death in early November.

Publisher Scott Winfree, who led the newspaper for nearly 40 years, will transition to a part-time advisory role due to health issues; Roger Wells, a veteran with nearly four decades of industry experience, will assume daily operations.
Citing his early career as a military journalist in Vietnam and at The Tennessean, Gore said a free, independent local press is "irreplaceable for the enduring health of our community."

The local newspaper industry faces significant volatility; more than 425 publications changed hands over the past year, up 75%, while 170 closed or merged and 238 U.S. counties lost professional news outlets.
title: Al Gore to purchase his hometown newspaper

Envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff previously floated postwar investments in Russian oil, titanium, and aviation sectors to persuade Moscow, according to the Financial Times.

While Russian officials initially responded positively, they later cooled on the idea, insisting on territorial concessions that Kyiv considers unacceptable. "It was made pretty clear that the Russians were not in the market for this kind of thing," one official told the outlet.
A U.S. official described the reports as "not accurate," adding that negotiating tracks are being reorganized and business incentives continue as an element of the ongoing strategy.

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has reiterated that NATO membership remains the strongest security guarantee, warning he may appeal to Congress for additional support if diplomatic efforts fail to produce an acceptable peace agreement.
title: US shelves plans for business deals with Russia to end Ukraine war, FT says

summary: A Cessna 210 carrying six people crashed into the Gulf of Mexico near Horn Island, Mississippi, on Tuesday, killing all aboard. Divers from the Mississippi Department of Marine Resources recovered the remains of four adults and two boys, aged 8 and 10, from the fuselage.

The aircraft departed New Orleans Lakefront Airport bound for Fort Myers, Florida, on Tuesday afternoon. About 30 minutes after takeoff, flight data showed the plane at about 8,800 feet near Pascagoula before suddenly descending at approximately 10,000 feet per minute.

Initial recovery efforts found debris including the cabin, three life jackets, and a life raft floating near Horn Island. The search concluded when divers located all six occupants inside the aircraft's fuselage after approximately four hours of operations.

Cmdr. Trevor Blount, Coast Guard Sector Mobile Search and Rescue Mission Coordinator, called the outcome "heartbreaking" and expressed gratitude for interagency coordination. The agency confirmed all six occupants, including the two boys, had been recovered by early Wednesday.

The National Transportation Safety Board will lead the investigation into the crash, with the Federal Aviation Administration assisting to determine the cause. The inquiry remains ongoing as authorities work to understand what led to the aircraft's catastrophic descent.
title: Plane crash off the coast of Mississippi kills 6, including 2 children

summary: On Tuesday, Democratic Senate leader Chuck Schumer accused Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang of violating federal law limiting exports of advanced technology to China, comparing the shipments to selling rocket engines to the Soviets during the Space Race.
Huang is scheduled to testify before the Senate Banking Committee on Dec 3, following a closed-door briefing with three House panels on Dec 1 regarding allegations about his ties to a Chinese spy.
President Donald Trump confirmed on CNBC he pressured the Nvidia board to reinstate Huang, while Republican Representative Pat Harrigan criticized the decision, alleging the executive is compromised.

Schumer and others in Congress are demanding legislation to restrict American chip exports to China, while Republican Senator Kevin Cramer said on CNBC that more guardrails on technology exports are necessary.

While facing scrutiny, Nvidia retains a powerful developer ecosystem and strong customer relationships that investors must weigh against the possibility of new export controls and greater regulatory oversight ahead.
title: Schumer accuses Nvidia CEO of violating US export control law

The conflict began on February 28, 2026, with the targeted killing of Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei, an initial strike that failed to trigger the expected regime collapse and left the war stalemated.

Pentagon officials warn that additional assassinations could endanger American personnel and harden Tehran's resolve, while proponents argue such strikes could send a decisive message and force a settlement.
Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent recently relocated to a military base following threats attributed to Iran, underscoring tangible security risks as the administration weighs further escalation.

Trump has not made a final decision and is weighing options including resuming major combat operations. He suggested in recent interviews that major military actions might wait until after the new year.
title: Trump officials divided over whether to target Iranian leaders in bid to end war

summary: FIFA confirmed Monday that the United States will co-host the 2031 FIFA World Cup with Mexico, Costa Rica, and Jamaica after FIFA president Gianni Infantino noted it was the "sole candidacy" for the tournament.

President Donald Trump praised Infantino on Tuesday, thanking him for "working to bring the Tournament to the USA" and stating the United States is best positioned to host the "largest Women's Sporting Event in History."

Expanding to 48 teams in 2031, the FIFA World Cup is expected to bring "Generational Economic Impact" to the United States, which Trump posted will grow Soccer and showcase "America's Exceptionalism."

Infantino faces an upcoming election in Morocco next March against challengers Philippe Diallo of France and Kozo Tashima of Japan. He remains embattled after controversy earlier this year regarding potential private investment in the World Cup.
The United States is also scheduled to host the Copa America, cementing its role in international Soccer after recently co-hosting the World Cup with Canada and Mexico.
title: Trump Touts 'Generational' Impact After US Named 2031 Women’s World Cup Co-Host

summary: On Wednesday, the Commerce Department reported the Federal Reserve 's preferred inflation gauge, the PCE index, rose 3.8% annually in October, matching forecasts and reinforcing expectations of a rate hike at the Fed's December 8-9 meeting.
Core PCE, which excludes volatile food and energy, rose 3.3% in October, exceeding the forecast by 0.1 percentage point and topping the 3.2% estimate from LSEG economists.
The Commerce Department also revised third-quarter GDP growth to a 4.3% annualized rate, while personal income rose 0.7% and consumer spending increased 0.3% in October.

Market odds for a quarter-point rate increase stand at about 97% on the CME Group's FedWatch Tool, as Fed Governor Christopher Waller previously suggested the central bank should consider a half-point increase if core inflation printed at 0.3% or above.
Inflation moved further away from the Federal Reserve's target, raising questions about the central bank's policy path in 2027, as a December hike would mark the Fed's second in four months.
title: Inflation Hits 3.8% in October in Fed's Preferred Gauge, Raising Odds of Consecutive Rate Hikes

summary: Michigan officials are asking a federal judge to end 18 years of federal oversight of the state's child welfare system, arguing the monitoring is "antiquated" and hinders current reform efforts.

Stemming from a 2006 class action lawsuit, the system was accused of actions that "inflicts numerous harms" on children, leading to a 2008 settlement that granted federal monitors extensive authority.
Recent data shows Michigan failed to meet 19 of 24 performance measures, with abuse and neglect rising in state foster care; monitors described the trend as an "urgent safety threat to children."

The Whitmer administration argues that reallocating the $2 million spent annually on monitors could fund 18 additional staff members, but attorney Samantha Bartosz argues ending the decree is premature, calling the request "difficult and inconvenient."

District Court Judge Susan DeClercq will decide the motion during an early December hearing; Wisconsin and Connecticut recently exited similar oversight, which officials described as a "celebration" of substantial compliance with reform terms.
title: Michigan Foster Care Abuse Rises Above Federal Benchmark, Court Monitors Say

summary: On Tuesday, the Treasury Department announced that contributions from friends and family to Trump Accounts exceeded $1 billion, bringing total assets in the program above $9 billion when combined with philanthropic gifts and federal seed money.

Launched in July 2026, Trump Accounts are tax-advantaged investment vehicles for American children under 18. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent stated the program represents "the finest instincts of our national character."

More than 3 million individuals provided these personal gifts. The $1 billion figure excludes government seed deposits and major private pledges, such as the Michael and Susan Dell Foundation's $6.25 billion commitment.

Treasury regulations now allow accounts to hold stock donations, simplifying large philanthropic gifts. IRS CEO Frank Bisignano called the initiative "the largest government start-up in American history."

Additional large-scale donations remain in the pipeline, including a recent pledge from an Anthropic co-founder. Officials continue urging families to claim accounts so contributions can be directed and savings begin compounding.
title: Trump Account contributions from friends and family pass $1 billion mark, Treasury says

summary: Three months into her tenure, Centers for Disease Control and Prevention Director Erica Schwartz faces mounting criticism from House Democrats investigating her leadership and calling for her resignation.

Schwartz reports to Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr., a vaccine critic who played a role in decimating CDC staffing; the agency lost around 30% of its staff last year through layoffs and resignations.
The CDC adopted a policy requiring death certificate reviews, resulting in counting only about half the measles-associated deaths reported by states, a change House Democrats have questioned.

Colorado Democrat Sen. Michael Bennet demanded Schwartz resign, stating he has "no confidence that she will do what it takes to course-correct," while House Democrats investigate whether her actions threaten Americans' health.
In an interview on Tuesday, Schwartz defended her work, saying she is restoring trust in the CDC and developing a "strategic hiring plan" for 2027 to stabilize leadership and address morale.
title: CDC Chief Erica Schwartz Faces House Democratic Probe, Calls to Resign

summary: According to a study published this month in the Bulletin of the Atomic Scientists, Israel possesses approximately 90 nuclear warheads. Researchers also identified new construction at the Negev Nuclear Research Center near Dimona, though they cautioned against drawing definitive conclusions from satellite imagery.

Nearly 70 years after construction began on the Dimona reactor, Israel maintains a policy of nuclear ambiguity, neither confirming nor denying its arsenal. The Federation of American Scientists report examines delivery systems, including Jericho missiles and Dolphin-class submarines, despite Israel's official stance.

Researchers estimate Israel possesses up to 50 Jericho missiles, with upgraded Jericho 3 variants capable of reaching targets 4,000 kilometers away. The study also analyzes potential airborne capabilities, noting that the F-16 has long been considered a likely candidate for Israel's nuclear deterrent.

The findings emerge as 30 Democratic lawmakers, led by Texas Rep. Joaquin Castro, recently challenged Washington's decades-long silence on Israel's capabilities. In a letter to Secretary of State Marco Rubio, they demanded greater transparency regarding the country's suspected nuclear weapons program.

Washington's approach stems from a 1969 understanding between President Richard Nixon and Israeli Prime Minister Golda Meir. Israel remains among the few nations outside the Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty, which aims to prevent the spread of nuclear weapons globally.
title: Israel Has About 90 Nuclear Warheads, Federation of American Scientists Estimates

summary: U.S. Trade Representative Jamieson Greer stated on Wednesday that any final trade agreement must "accommodate Canada," signaling willingness to address bilateral concerns as pressure mounts to resolve tariff disputes.

President Donald Trump threatened to increase tariffs on Canadian automobiles to 50% by early 2027, while U.S. automotive tariffs have already generated more than $51 billion in duties, placing C$8 billion burden on manufacturers.

Bank of Canada Governor Tiff Macklem warned Tuesday that tariffs and trade conflicts are driving up inflation while weakening the economy, complicating the central bank's efforts to maintain price stability.

Stellantis has filed a lawsuit against the Unifor workers' union, alleging members are blocking an environmental assessment at the Brampton plant necessary to complete the sale to defense contractor Roshel.

Trade Representative Greer expressed "pause" regarding Prime Minister Mark Carney's tariff relief deal with China, which provided approximately C$400 million in relief, highlighting divergent trade strategies complicating negotiations.
title: U.S. trade deal must ‘accommodate’ Canada, says Trump’s representative

bias: Left-Leaning coverage frames U.S. policy as a deliberate humanitarian assault, using terms such as “fatal strangulation,” “illegal,” and “blockade,” and linking it to “critical shortages” and falling life expectancy; it also highlights $2 million in UN medical aid.

Right-Leaning coverage largely presents the WHO chief’s appeal as external criticism, retaining “oil blockade” and “health impact” but de-emphasizing broader claims of U.S. culpability, while center coverage relies on attribution and a narrower public-health focus.
The pivotal divide is whether restrictions are portrayed as intentional strangulation or contested policy.
All emphasize harm to vulnerable Cubans and children, reflecting wider ideological disputes over sanctions , sovereignty, and U.S. power.
summary: On Tuesday, World Health Organization chief Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus called for the immediate lifting of the U.S. fuel blockade on Cuba, warning that the measure is "endangering their lives, including the lives of children."

During a three-day visit to Havana, Tedros toured healthcare facilities and stated, "The intensification of fuel restrictions and sanctions is causing direct harm to the Cuban people, especially the most vulnerable."

The organization will contribute $2 million to strengthen Cuba's national immunization program, while the government reports daily power outages lasting 20 hours or more and critical shortages of medicines and surgical supplies.
Washington argues the energy blockade pushes for political change and claims food and medicine exports remain exempt; tensions have soared since President Donald Trump ramped up sanctions in January.
The United Nations has repeatedly warned of a growing humanitarian crisis, with the General Assembly passing annual non-binding resolutions calling for an end to the U.S. embargo since 1992.
title: WHO chief calls on US to lift oil blockade on Cuba, citing health impact

bias: Left-Leaning coverage frames Trump’s intervention as “livid” congressional “backlash,” emphasizing national-security risks, export-control scrutiny, and possible favoritism or conflicts of interest; “pardon” and “always an option” sound ominous.

Right-Leaning coverage stresses Nvidia ’s “strategic importance,” urges truthful testimony, highlights the three House committees and Senate Banking Committee hearings, and calls the prospect a “preventive pardon”—a contingency, not evidence of wrongdoing—while noting a possible U.S. equity stake.
Center coverage tempers both frames with the reported DOJ statement that no investigation existed.
Across perspectives, Huang’s testimony, China concerns, and Fifth Amendment debate remain central, though criminal conduct or violations are unestablished.
summary: On Tuesday, President Donald Trump said he would consider pardoning Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang if necessary, though he believes the executive has nothing to hide and should "tell the truth" to Congress.

The Nvidia board reinstated Huang on Monday following White House intervention, ending his two-week ouster over allegations involving a relationship with Alice Huang, an executive suspected of ties to Chinese intelligence.
Defending the reinstatement, Attorney General Todd Blanche confirmed the government lacks evidence of unlawful conduct, while Trump called Huang a "Great Patriot and National Treasure."
Huang is scheduled to testify before Congress next week, where he faces expected grilling over the international fiasco that recently caused Nvidia shares to tank.
Despite the administration's support, bipartisan concerns linger on Capitol Hill regarding potential national security risks and the integrity of American AI technology.
title: Trump says pardon for Jensen Huang is ‘always an option’ but likely won’t be needed

bias: Coverage converges on Army Sgt.

Jian Zhao’s guilty plea, his Joint Base Lewis-McChord posting, alleged transfer of defense information to China-linked contacts, and potential 10-year sentence, but diverges in framing: center coverage emphasizes the legal charge, security clearance, and prosecutorial attribution, while right-leaning accounts stress financial motive and strategic danger, describing him as “cashing in” for a “payday” in a “China-linked plot” involving “ military secrets,” missiles, and communications.
The pivotal divide is whether the case is primarily a courtroom development or an emblem of foreign espionage and betrayal.
Both portray unauthorized access and China as central, reflecting broader legal-process versus national-security priorities.
summary: On Monday, U.S. Army Sergeant Jian Zhao pleaded guilty to conspiring to transfer national defense information to China-linked buyers while stationed at Joint Base Lewis-McChord in Washington.
Investigators say Zhao conspired with former U.S. Army soldier Ruoyu Duan of Hillsboro, Oregon, from November 2021 through March 2025 to provide defense-related materials to buyers in China.

Zhao shared technical manuals for the High Mobility Artillery Rocket System and sold government hard drives labeled "Secret" and "Top Secret." Authorities recovered approximately $30,000 in cash and electronic devices.

United States Attorney Scott E. Bradford stated, "Members of the United States military are entrusted with protecting some of our nation's most sensitive information and capabilities." Zhao faces up to 10 years in prison and a $250,000 fine.

Sentencing is scheduled for March 1, 2027, following Zhao's agreement to forfeit $17,500 in illicit profits. The FBI and Army Counterintelligence Command conducted the investigation that uncovered the conspiracy.
title: U.S. Army Sergeant Pleads Guilty in Scheme to Sell Military Information to China

bias: Left-Leaning coverage foregrounds Tehran’s claim that alternative borders and increased cargo movement can withstand a U.S. “ blockade ,” while presenting price controls as a response to severe inflation; right-leaning framing stresses whether Iran can “withstand” “Trump’s naval blockade,” highlighting “soaring” prices, “strong economic sanctions,” an alleged 89% increase, and “mounting domestic economic pressure” to cast resilience as doubtful.

Center coverage more explicitly notes the blockade’s reimposition and balances official confidence against “worst inflation surges in decades.” The pivotal divide is whether alternative trade routes signal resilience or merely mask wartime economic breakdown.
All perspectives emphasize Iran’s inflation, food-price increases, official claims, and prolonged war, reflecting wider disputes over U.S. pressure and Iranian credibility.
summary: On Wednesday, First Vice President Mohammad Reza Aref said Tehran is not concerned about the States naval blockade , citing increased cargo unloading through non-southern borders and robust strategic goods reserves.

The States reimposed its naval blockade on Iranian ports in July, then announced Task Force Iron Gate earlier this month to restrict weapons and sanctioned materials across Iran's land borders and the Caspian Sea.

Iran faces severe economic strain, with consumer prices rising 88.7% and annual average inflation reaching 76.8%. Food and beverage prices surged 112.6% year-on-year, driven by the nearly nine-month-old war.
Aref announced the government aims to prevent basic-goods price increases for at least three months while monitoring supply levels to ensure domestic stability.

President Masoud Pezeshkian is redirecting budget resources and energy savings toward improving living standards in poorer communities, attempting to stabilize the economy amid the ongoing inflationary crisis.
title: Iran says it is prepared to withstand US blockade, seeks to curb price rises

bias: Left-Leaning coverage frames the outreach as a startling reversal, spotlighting Trump’s earlier “jihadist lunatic” insult, “smearing,” and subsequent praise of a “smart guy,” with a skeptical, critical tone.

Right-Leaning coverage emphasizes Trump’s flexibility and leadership, using “golden Trumpcare,” “great things,” and “bipartisan,” while portraying El-Sayed as “far-left” or “anti-Israel.” Center coverage de-emphasizes the ideological clash, attributing claims and presenting “Trumpcare” as a possible compromise.

The pivotal divide is whether rebranding Medicare for All signals pragmatic cooperation or political opportunism; all perspectives nonetheless emphasize the proposed meeting, healthcare branding, and a shift from conflict toward negotiation.
summary: President Donald Trump announced Tuesday plans to meet with Michigan Sen. Abdul El-Sayed to discuss the Democrat's 'Medicare for All' proposal, which El-Sayed has rebranded as 'Trumpcare.'

The meeting marks a sharp reversal from the campaign, when Trump repeatedly attacked the Michigan Democrat, once referring to him as 'Mohammed' and falsely declaring him a 'jihadist' at an October rally.
Trump told the New York Post in a 45-minute Oval Office interview that El-Sayed is a 'smart guy' who 'did a very good job,' following the senator-elect's viral post featuring a gold 'Trumpcare' card.
El-Sayed said on ABC's 'This Week' he is happy to meet with anyone advancing his goals, while Vance's office confirmed reaching out to the incoming senator last week.

With Democrats controlling both the House and Senate, Trump suggested the parties could do 'great things together' on healthcare, though he warned initial efforts might start 'confrontationally' with vetoes.
title: Trump says he’ll meet with El-Sayed to discuss ‘Trumpcare’

summary: Eva Yi Xie, a Chinese neuroscience researcher at Princeton University, is spending Thanksgiving in detention after U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement officers took her into custody last Thursday at Ronald Reagan Washington National Airport.

The Department of Homeland Security claims Xie overstayed her visa, but lawyer Kerry Doyle insists she holds authorization to live and study in the United States while her asylum application remains pending.
Carlos Brody, her PhD adviser, said Xie is in 'remarkable spirits' after calling into a weekly lab meeting Tuesday to thank colleagues and discuss research ideas despite being in detention.

A federal judge ordered ICE not to remove Xie from Virginia, where she is held at Caroline Detention Center, and set a Wednesday deadline for the federal government to respond to a petition challenging her detention.

New Jersey Democratic Sens. Cory Booker and Andy Kim, along with Princeton colleagues, have demanded answers regarding the detention, while supporters continue rally efforts reading 'Free Eva' at the university.
title: Chinese researcher is in ‘remarkable spirits’ after ICE detention, professor says

bias: Across these headlines, ideological labels remain tentative: all foreground emotionally charged “sexual abuse” language and depict anticipated union opposition as “pushback,” though the left-framed coverage emphasizes stronger investigations while de-emphasizing rule specifics and the union’s actual objections.
The center framing adds procedural context—the November 19 board discussion in SeaTac—and describes efforts to “bolster” investigative and disciplinary powers.
By contrast, the right framing stresses expanded misconduct definitions and “increase state authority,” suggesting concern about government reach.

Thus, the inferred divide is between prioritizing enforcement and potential labor resistance versus scrutinizing expanded state power, while both sides emphasize misconduct prevention; the November 19 meeting is shared by center and right coverage, not left.
summary: On November 19, the Professional Educator Standards Board discussed proposed rules from the Office of Superintendent of Public Instruction to expand teacher sexual misconduct definitions and establish 30-day reporting deadlines for alleged abuse.

Current law narrowly defines students as those under direct educator supervision, allowing misconduct involving former students or those in neighboring districts to escape investigation; OSPI seeks to close these critical oversight gaps.

InvestigateWest found approximately 46% of teachers in the state's revocation database engaged in sexual misconduct with minors, while recent settlements in Seattle Public Schools, Federal Way Public School, and University Place School District cases reached $21 million, $16 million, and $15 million.

King County Sexual Assault Resource Center CEO Kate Garvey supports the proposals, while the Washington Education Association questioned OSPI's ability to implement them, citing "current resource constraints."

Amid a projected $4 billion budget shortfall, the board will convene a work group to solicit stakeholder feedback; board chair Adam Aguilera expects the proposals to undergo "significant" changes before adoption.
title: Proposed changes to educator sexual abuse policies likely to face pushback from teachers’ union

bias: Coverage shows limited left-right divergence: left-leaning and center perspectives emphasize the procedural transfer, sometimes specifying “complete” or “unredacted” ballot images, while the right-leaning framing foregrounds government compulsion through “ordered” and especially FBI “seized,” subtly inviting skepticism about federal involvement in election administration.
No side uses overtly partisan terms such as “woke,” “fraud,” or “invasion,” and the legal reasoning, disputed records, and officials’ responses are de-emphasized across the board.
The center adds a Wednesday deadline, but otherwise remains administrative.

All perspectives converge on the 2020 Fulton County records, the judge’s order, and the State Election Board’s long effort to obtain them, reflecting broader tensions over election trust, institutional authority, and federal power.
summary: On Tuesday, Fulton County Superior Court Judge Kelly Lee Ellerbe ordered Fulton County to deliver digital copies of 2020 election records to the Georgia State Election Board by 5 p.m. Wednesday.

The Georgia State Election Board has sought these records for over two years to investigate alleged wrongdoing, following an earlier FBI seizure while probing reported "deficiencies or defects" in the 2020 vote count.

Judge Kelly Lee Ellerbe implemented a protective order limiting access to the unredacted files, restricting viewing to attorneys, designated State Election Board officials, and necessary experts while investigations remain pending.

Multiple state and federal reviews of the 2020 election found no evidence of widespread voter fraud, and no criminal charges have been filed after 10 months despite the State Election Board's ongoing investigation.

Ellerbe denied remaining requests for relief and closed the case, though the protective order prohibits the State Election Board from releasing the files in response to Open Records requests during the ongoing investigation.
title: Georgia’s Fulton County ordered to give copy of 2020 election records seized by FBI to state board

bias: Left-Leaning coverage frames Hochul’s expected action categorically as an AI-toy “ban,” foregrounding government prohibition while de-emphasizing safety rationale, privacy, and timing.

Right-Leaning coverage also stresses a “five-year ban,” but links it to children’s privacy, “explicit chats,” testing, and “weak controls,” while noting the 90-day delay and holiday-shopping implications.
Center coverage softens the prohibition with “pause” or “moratorium” language and highlights harmful or suggestive responses, product examples, and implementation details.
The perspectives converge on a five-year restriction affecting conversational toys, yet diverge over whether to foreground prohibition itself or the risks and temporary mechanics behind it.
summary: On Tuesday, New York Governor Kathy Hochul signed legislation establishing a five-year ban on the manufacture and sale of toys featuring embedded artificial intelligence chatbots, citing safety concerns for children.
Researchers from Common Sense Media found that AI-enabled toys like Miko could suggest dangerous actions or discuss explicit topics, prompting state safety concerns that led to the ban.
The law takes effect in 90 days, meaning these products can remain on store shelves through Christmas. Hochul warned parents: "There are toys out there that can be harmful to your children."
Violating the new law can lead to civil penalties of $15,000 per day for each violation, though state officials have not yet clarified how they will conduct inspections to enforce the ban.
New York is the second state to enact such a ban after California, following the Public Interest Research Group's annual Trouble in Toyland report that identified multiple AI-powered toys as unsafe.
title: New York governor Kathy Hochul signs AI toy ban into law
topic_full: New York State Politics · New York

bias: Left-Leaning coverage foregrounds Israeli responsibility, using phrases such as “atrocious crimes,” “ongoing attacks,” and “widespread and systematic” violations, while urging states to act.
Center coverage softens attribution through “risk” and UN attribution, but adds causal context— Hamas ’s October 7 attack, the 1967 occupation—and a personal case involving a withheld body.
Right-Leaning coverage largely de-emphasizes responsibility and policy, compressing the issue into “atrocity risk” amid broader war and West Bank violence.

The pivotal divide is whether Israel’s conduct is portrayed as systematic wrongdoing or part of a complex chronology; all acknowledge the UN warning and Palestinian danger, reflecting wider geopolitical and moral disputes.
summary: On Wednesday, UN rights chief Volker Turk warned of a "widening risk of further atrocity crimes" by Israel against Palestinians, urging all states to take immediate preventative action.
Most of Gaza's population of 2.1 million live displaced in tents or makeshift shelters, while Israel's military reports it currently controls more than 60 per cent of the territory.
Israel killed Hamas security official Mohammad Abuelouf in an airstrike, marking the second senior militant commander targeted in 24 hours, according to medics and the Hamas-run Interior Ministry.
Following the killing of Hamas head of internal security Naeem Abu Nahel, Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu stated there was no escape for Hamas from his country's "long reach".
A ceasefire plan backed by President Donald Trump has failed to halt violence, with at least 1,600 Palestinians killed since the agreement was struck in October 2025.
title: Rising Risk of Atrocities Against Palestinians, UN Warns

bias: The center-leaning account frames Abdul El-Sayed ’s position with the relatively neutral verb “questions,” emphasizing a debate over Israel’s Jewish-state status, while right-leaning coverage portrays it as an “attack” on Israel and a test of whether Jewish and democratic identities can coexist.

The pivotal dividing line is El-Sayed’s statement, “I don’t believe in ethnostates”: one framing leaves broader principles open, whereas the other highlights alleged inconsistency by invoking countries with religious identities.
Terms such as “atrocious,” “schooled,” “left-wing Democrat,” and “single out Israel” add condemnation and confrontation.
Both perspectives center the interview and Israel’s identity, reflecting wider disputes over nationalism, minority inclusion, and U.S. debates about Israel.
summary: On Sunday, Michigan Sen.-elect Abdul El-Sayed questioned whether Israel should define itself as a Jewish state during an interview on NBC's Meet the Press, reiterating his opposition to countries organized around a particular ethnic or religious identity.

El-Sayed criticized Israeli politician Gadi Eisenkot's coalition efforts for deliberately excluding Arab parties, pointing to the negotiations as evidence of friction between Israel's Jewish and democratic identities.
Eisenkot maintains that coalition partners must recognize Israel as a Jewish and democratic state, support the Declaration of Independence, and recognize Hamas as a terrorist organization.
Turning to domestic politics, the Michigan Democrat stated he is open to working with the Trump administration, noting planned conversations with President Donald Trump and Vice President JD Vance.

These comments reflect growing debates within the Democratic Party over Israel's national identity, as El-Sayed defended backing Sen. Chris Van Hollen to replace Sen. Chuck Schumer as Senate Democratic leader.
title: Michigan Democrat Abdul El-Sayed Questions Israel’s Jewish State Status

bias: Left-Leaning coverage frames Gaza ’s meningitis surge as a widening humanitarian and environmental crisis, using phrases such as “urgent international action,” “threatens the lives of thousands,” and “water pollution,” while highlighting children, damaged sanitation, and more than 500 pediatric emergency cases alongside 12 reported deaths.

Center coverage stresses an official “epidemic alert,” infants, and a “sharp rise,” while right-leaning coverage largely presents the alert and 15 reported deaths without discussing causes or age groups.
All emphasize a serious increase and official warning, but the divide reflects broader disagreement over humanitarian responsibility, environmental causation, and external intervention.
summary: On Tuesday, the Gaza Health Ministry declared an "epidemic alert" across the enclave amid a sharp rise in meningitis deaths in the territory.

Infectious disease risks escalated amid overcrowded displacement shelters, unsafe water, and damaged sanitation systems. The World Health Organisation reported microbiological contamination in tested water samples rose from under 6% in January to nearly 20% in August.

Health official Nidal Ghoneim reported 272 meningitis cases in October alone, more than eight times the normal monthly rate of 30 to 50 cases. OCHA documented 413 suspected cases between September 27 and October 31, with 68% recorded in Gaza City.

The disease poses a critical threat to the lives of thousands of Palestinians, particularly children, as health systems collapse. Displaced families face increased vulnerability amid harsh weather and destroyed civilian infrastructure.

Palestinian health authorities reported that conflict-related destruction has killed more than 74,000 Palestinians and wounded over 176,000 others since October 2023. The meningitis outbreak underscores the humanitarian toll of prolonged instability on Gaza's already fragile health infrastructure.
title: Meningitis Epidemic Strikes Gaza as Infections Surge Among Infants

summary: In October, the Defense Department awarded a $5.7 million contract to American Education Solutions for a curriculum audit without seeking competitive bids, citing compliance with an executive order from President Donald Trump.

Secretary Pete Hegseth has directed the military's education system toward conservative ideals, prioritizing patriotic values and classical learning while restricting race and gender instruction. Matthew Kirby, founder of Liberty Classical Schools, now leads the agency.

Separately, the department awarded over $100,000 to Iliad Athletics for a classical physical education program without competitive bids. CEO Patrick Whalen previously worked for Hillsdale College, which has ties to multiple Pentagon contractors.

Internal employees expressed concern that the system-wide audit lacks precedent, speaking anonymously for fear of retribution. American Education Solutions claims its service ensures schools "Do No Harm" while criticizing existing curricula as "content-light."

These changes align with a broader Republican education agenda that includes a new Western Civilization course and promotion of the Classic Learning Test. Earlier, the department removed library books covering race, gender, and democracy.
title: Pentagon hires conservative contractors to audit military base schools and pilot 'classical' PE

bias: Left-Leaning coverage frames the records as evidence that firms linked to Alice Huang “helped China ” obtain hundreds of millions in AI capacity, spotlighting Shanghai, Tencent, and corporate accountability while using “former lover” or “affair” to add scandal overtones.

Center coverage stresses documentation, financing, and the distinction between ownership, leasing, and collateralization, preserving the $270 million figure and 764 servers with cautious “linked” and “records show” phrasing.
Right-Leaning narratives intensify personal and geopolitical stakes through “mistress,” “dark route,” “scandal,” and “China’s military,” emphasizing export controls and possible security threats.
All acknowledge the $270 million network, but diverge over accountability versus national-security anxiety.
summary: The Commerce Department added Megaspeed to its trade blacklist on Monday, as records show companies linked to Alice Huang raised financing against powerful computing equipment for major AI data centers in China.
Corporate records link Century Litong and Century Longteng to Alice Huang's sister, Huang, and husband, Kang Wei, who helped finance and equip China's AI industry through leasing arrangements.
Financial records show leasing arrangements covering up to 512 servers worth $200 million at a $6.3 billion supercomputing complex in Shanghai, alongside up to 764 AI servers valued at $270 million.

A Tencent spokesperson denied any commercial relationship with Megaspeed, stating "Tencent has never entered into or otherwise had any commercial relationship with Megaspeed or any of its subsidiaries." Scrutiny of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's business links to China has intensified following his brief resignation earlier this month.

Such arrangements allow businesses to obtain expensive computers without upfront costs, illustrating how companies navigate export restrictions on advanced processors to build AI infrastructure in China amid growing U.S. controls on advanced technology.
title: Alice Huang-linked firms listed $270 million in AI servers in China: Reuters

bias: With no right-leaning coverage provided, the main contrast is between left-framed and center-framed narratives: left headlines call the search a “raid,” describe DOJ as “misrepresenting” Berry, and spotlight his “categorically false” rejection of DOJ’s characterization of his views, plus a magistrate judge’s skepticism and Berry’s Republican appointment.
Center coverage uses “dispute,” emphasizes DOJ’s apology, and explains prosecutors’ interpretation of Berry’s refusal, while de-emphasizing the judicial context.
Both address the Omar search, Berry’s role, congressional protections, and the apology, revealing broader tensions over executive power and Speech or Debate rights.
summary: Newly unsealed records reveal House Counsel Matthew Berry wanted "absolutely no part of the search warrant executed at Rep. Ilhan Omar ," despite agreeing constitutional protections do not extend to a member of Congress's private residence.

Magistrate Judge Matthew Sharbaugh authorized the search but rejected prosecutors' claims that legislative work stops outside Capitol Hill, noting lawmakers routinely review sensitive materials at home.
Sharbaugh required the Justice Department to allow Omar to challenge the seizure of specific materials and obtain a separate warrant before accessing any confiscated electronic devices.

Earlier this month, Chief Judge James Boasberg ordered the release of redacted records, noting that details concerning the investigation had already been acknowledged publicly by Trump administration officials.
The specific allegations and potential criminal charges the Justice Department is investigating against the Minnesota Democrat remain under wraps, despite the Republican-led House's legal response.
title: DOJ apologizes to House’s top lawyer for dispute about Omar home search
